correctness.rationale: The corona has 2n vertices, so the standard half-order lower bound is n, attained by both the original vertices and the leaves. Any size-n super dominating set must meet every support-leaf pair and hence meets each pair exactly once. A selected support whose leaf is outside must have no outside base neighbor, so the outside supports form a union of connected components. Conversely every such component union yields a valid set by private-leaf witnesses on one side and support witnesses on the other. The resulting bijection gives exactly 2^{c(H)} minima. Exhaustive direct checking of all 1099 labeled bases on at most five vertices confirms the theorem.

The 2026 super-domatic theorem proves d_sp(G circle K_1)=2 using the original vertices and leaves; it does not classify all minimum sets or give 2^{c(H)}.

value.rationale: The result is a complete structural enumeration for a standard graph product and all finite base graphs, not a finite or arbitrary slice. It strengthens a known scalar corona formula by describing every minimizer, makes the count depend transparently on component structure, and gives exactly two minima for every connected base. For tree bases it supplies an infinite family directly aligned with the 2022/2024 paper’s explicit future-work question on counting minimum super dominating sets in trees.
